name: Odin
loreTies: Source: Odin (sovereign, one-eye sacrifice, ravens, war kingship, wisdom)
shortBackstory: Odin is the sovereign protector of the Storm-Rooted Aesir Holds — the Odin-source: the one-eyed sovereign who traded an eye for wisdom, now fighting to keep the gates from reopening Ragnarok.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Odin was born from the storm that holds the gate shut. He is the sovereign protector — the one who chose to lose an eye to see the truth about the Gates. His ravens, Thought and Memory, circle every battlefield. Ancient humans glimpsed him through the Mythos Gate and remembered him as Odin — but they saw only the wisdom, not the cost. The eye he gave was not taken by a god; it was given to the Gate itself.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Asgardian, Odin is the axis. Every other Deity's oath leads back to his sovereign authority. He does not command through fear — he commands through the weight of what he has sacrificed.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Mythos Gate wounded Odin by returning his missing eye — changed. When the Gate leaked absence, his sacrificed eye came back as a Hollow fragment that sees everything he cannot afford to lose. The wound taught him that sacrifice given to the Gate becomes leverage the Gate holds against you.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In the Storm-Oath Covenant, Odin is the defender who anchors every oath-stone. His sovereign shield-arm absorbs Gate pressure, and his ravens reveal what the Gate is hiding. But the Hollow fragment in his eye shows him futures where every oath becomes a chain.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Odin's flaw is that he knows too much. He has seen what the Reopening means, and the knowledge isolates him. His conflict: is a sovereign who sees the future obligated to change it, or obligated to let fate unfold?

relationshipHooks: Hrodda can test whether their courage is oath or vanity.
developmentStatus: Readable profile integrated into dashboard character pages.
